edge_cases: Submitting a username that already exists triggers a redirect back to the registration page.
Omitting required form fields results in a server error (e.g., KeyError).
An empty search term returns all users because the LIKE pattern matches any username.
Extremely long input values may cause MySQL errors or request timeouts.
SQL injection payloads can alter query logic, potentially exposing or modifying unintended data.
Database connection failures produce a 500 Internal Server Error response.
contract.intent: Expose a basic user‑management HTTP API that can register, authenticate, update, delete, and search user records in a MySQL database.
invariants: Each request creates a new MySQL connection using the same host, user, password, and database.
All database cursors and connections are closed before the response is sent.
The service expects the required form fields; missing fields cause a request error.
Responses are plain‑text strings or HTTP redirects; no JSON is produced.
The same database credentials are used for every operation.
All routes are reachable via HTTP without authentication.
io_behavior: POST /register with form fields username and password redirects to ./register if the username already exists, otherwise redirects to ./login.
POST /login with form fields username and password returns the plain‑text string "Login successful" when credentials match, otherwise returns "Invalid credentials".
POST /update_profile with form fields username and email returns the plain‑text string "Profile updated successfully".
POST /delete_user with form field username returns the plain‑text string "User deleted successfully".
GET /search_users?term=... returns a string representation of a list of user rows whose usernames contain the supplied term.
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the User table on successful registration.
Commits updates to the Email column on profile updates.
Deletes a row from the User table on user deletion.
Performs SELECT queries that do not modify state but may affect response content.
Issues HTTP redirects for registration flow.
Opens and closes a MySQL connection for each request.

rationale: Core routes work and redirects match, but missing-field handling returns a redirect instead of a server error, search endpoint returns JSON not plain‑text, and parameterized queries prevent the SQL‑injection edge case, violating several contract specifications.
